Stated Claim / Post Context:
Election 2026: Dogs at polling booths | The Spinoff

We're bringing you nothing but live pupdates till 7pm.

Actual Article Body:
Just some dogs excited about democracy. (Image: Tina Tiller/The Spinoff)

We're bringing you nothing but live pupdates till 7pm.

Stevie enjoyed her fourth NZ election this year, and third at the polls. The fourth was an overseas special vote. Welcome back, Stevie.

Six-year-old bearded collie Bessie has been enjoying a cozy Wellington city life while her less anxious siblings work on the farm. She very very bravely went to the polls in Brooklyn today for her last NZ election before moving to the UK (her ancestral land) with her family. Godspeed, Bessie.

Are you surprised? Look at her kind face. Hazel here loved everyone at the polling station in Little River.

This is Harley voting in Island Bay, where apparently there’s a "queue of dogs at the Presbyterian Church waiting to take their Spinoff photos". God/Dog bless you all.

This is Aster’s second election getting stuck in but all she wanted was a big bowl of cold water and a lie down because it’s so damn muggy outside. As an aside: I vote to get this dog an agent.

We've got Jem, we've got Falkor and we've got Moro. Two greyhounds and a whippet and I'm just going to guess that Moro is the whippet (vibes only). Destiny's Child here strutted over to Strathmore Park to get involved this election.

What's the difference between a spoodle and a sproodle? Genuine question because I'm not sure if one is a typo or if every breed has been mixed with a poodle at some point.

Anyway Maggie voted two ticks treats in Karori.

Nero helped their (no pronouns given but the harness gives they/them anyway) owner vote in Kaipara ki Mahurangi this morning.

"She’s been unsettled all week bolting out the gate, then later ended up settling in next to the voting sign," says Cindy's owner, having voted in Birkenhead with a very chill Cindy.

But she's still enthusiastic about the democratic process – and cheese. The 14-year-old lab voted at Vauxhall School in the North Shore electorate. Fantastic work, Freya.

Jimmy is a four-year-old black Aussiedor and Cassie is a one-year-old merle border collie, out for a soggy political walk in Westmere, Auckland. Really good posing from them.

Daisy the miniature schnauzer went for a walk in an undisclosed location and stumbled across a voting booth so decided to vote together. Sniffed the sign and declared it acceptable.

Did you pat a bearded collie x huntaway at St Francis of Assisi School, Mairehau, Christchurch? Well that was his whole plan, even if it was a bit hot to be...
